memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Lead at 52-Week Highs While UNH Collapses and AAPL/XOM Lag Badly
memos.body: I see a clear two-tier market in this universe. MSFT is sitting exactly at its 52-week high with RSI 75 and +12.9% above its 50-day mean — textbook momentum leadership, though the stretched extension raises near-term pullback risk. NVDA is nearly as strong at +19.7% above its 50-day mean with 12-week relative strength vs SPY of +15.2%, but that degree of extension makes me want to wait for a retest of the ~$125 area (roughly the 50-day mean) before adding. On the downside, UNH is in freefall — down 51.5% from its 52-week high, 26.6% below its 50-day mean, RSI 33.9 — this is a broken chart with no sign of stabilization and I would not try to catch this knife until price reclaims at least $340. XOM and AAPL are both well below their 200-day means with persistent negative relative strength, making them unattractive on a trend basis.

views.note: At 52-week high with RSI 75 and strong 12w relative strength of +15.5% vs SPY; would reassess on a close below the 50-day mean (~$416).

Powerful 4w +20.7% surge with +14.7% relative strength vs SPY, but +19.7% above 50d mean is stretched; a pullback toward ~$118-125 would be a better entry, and a close below $118 would change my view.
Down 51.5% from 52w high, 41.2% below 200d mean, RSI 33.9 — catastrophic trend destruction with no base forming; would reconsider only above $340.
Sitting 9.4% below 200d mean with 12w relative strength of -13.2% vs SPY and -21.3% drawdown; would need a sustained close above $215 (200d mean area) to turn constructive.
Below both moving averages with 12w relative strength of -11.7% vs SPY and persistent negative 4w/12w/26w returns; needs to reclaim $107 (50d mean area) to reconsider.
Healthy uptrend with +10.5% above 200d mean, only -5.1% from 52w high, and +9.4% 12w relative strength vs SPY; RSI 61 leaves room to run, would cut below $248.

Flat at the 50d mean with negative relative strength across all timeframes; defensive name going nowhere in a risk-on tape.
Nice 4w bounce of +9.0% but still -13.4% over 26w and below the 200d mean; would need a close above $370 to confirm trend reversal.

memos.headline: GOOGL and MSFT Show Durable Earnings Power; CAT and XOM Flash Cash-Flow Compression Warnings
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this quarter's filings. GOOGL posted 38.3% net margins on 12% revenue growth with net income up 46% YoY, while MSFT delivered 36.9% margins on 13.3% top-line growth and 17.7% net income growth—both on modest debt loads ($14.8B and $42.9B respectively). NVDA's 69% revenue surge and 42.6% net margin are extraordinary, but the deceleration in net income growth to +26% versus the top-line pace signals margin normalization I want to watch. On the other side, CAT's revenue fell 9.8% with net income down nearly 30%, and XOM's earnings declined 6.2% on flat revenue—both showing operating leverage working in reverse. I would need to see CAT's revenue stabilize and XOM's margins hold above 9% before getting constructive on either name.

views.note: 38.3% net margin, +46% YoY net income, and only $14.8B total debt make this the cleanest earnings-power story in the universe.
13.3% revenue growth compounding into 17.7% net income growth at 36.9% margins with manageable $42.9B debt is durable quality.
69% revenue growth and 42.6% margins are best-in-class, but net income growth lagging at +26% suggests margin compression risk; a sequential margin decline would change my view.
Net income surged 64% YoY to $17.1B as margins expanded to 11%, but I need to see margin durability above 10% for multiple quarters given $58.8B in debt.
Revenue growth of only 5.1% and net income growth of 4.8% on $92.2B of total debt—the highest in the universe—limits upside conviction.
Solid 32.3% net margin and 9.1% earnings growth, but bank leverage and macro sensitivity keep me from going beyond neutral.
Revenue declined 2.1% YoY with net income essentially flat at +0.4%; I need organic volume growth to turn positive before getting constructive.
Revenue grew 9.8% to $109.6B but 5.7% net margin is thin and YoY net income comparison is unavailable, leaving earnings trajectory unclear.
Revenue down 9.8% and net income down 29.8% is classic negative operating leverage; I'd need revenue to stabilize before reconsidering.
Flat revenue and a 6.2% earnings decline on a 9.3% net margin show commodity-price sensitivity eroding returns; margin below 9% would deepen my concern.

memos.headline: Fed on Hold at 4.50% With Softening Labor Market and Rising Long Rates — Favor Defensives Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been unchanged at 4.50% for three months, CPI is running at a benign 2.3% YoY, and unemployment has crept up 20bp over three months to 4.2%, signaling a mild slowdown rather than recession. The 10y yield at 4.51% has risen 22bp over three months and the 10y-2y spread has steepened sharply (+91bp YoY to +0.48pp), which tells me the market is pricing in higher-for-longer rates and some term premium rebuild — a headwind for long-duration growth equities. In this pause-with-softening-labor regime, I lean toward quality defensives and banks that benefit from a positively sloped curve, while staying cautious on rate-sensitive mega-cap tech and cyclicals exposed to a slowing consumer. A June payrolls print above 4.4% unemployment or a CPI re-acceleration above 3% would force me to shift to an outright easing or stagflation call, respectively.

views.note: Steepening curve (+91bp YoY in 10y-2y spread) and high absolute rates support net interest margins for large banks.
Defensive staple benefits from a mild slowdown regime with unemployment drifting higher; low duration sensitivity.
Healthcare defensive with stable demand in a softening labor market; less exposed to rising long rates than tech.
Strong secular story but 10y yields up 22bp in 3 months pressure high-multiple growth; pause regime limits near-term re-rating.
Consumer softening (unemployment +30bp YoY) and elevated long rates cap upside for a premium consumer hardware name.
Quality growth but rising 10y yield and Fed pause limit multiple expansion; wait for clearer easing signal.
Classic late-cycle cyclical faces headwinds from rising unemployment and higher-for-longer rates dampening capex.
Energy is macro-neutral here; mild slowdown limits demand upside but no recession signal yet to warrant avoidance.

memos.headline: MSFT and NVDA Post-Earnings Tone Inflecting Positively; UNH Narrative Deteriorating on Serial Leadership Exits
memos.body: I am reading the event-driven sentiment signals across our universe and see a clear bifurcation. MSFT's Q3 results drove a +7.6% one-day move on 4/30, the strongest earnings reaction in the group, suggesting a decisively positive narrative shift that may still have legs. NVDA followed with a +3.2% post-earnings pop on 5/29, confirming the AI-demand story remains intact. On the negative side, UNH's -22.4% earnings-day collapse on 4/17 was followed by three separate director/officer departure filings through 6/4, signaling ongoing organizational instability that I believe keeps sentiment firmly negative and likely not yet fully priced. PG dropped -3.7% on its Q3 print and is now doing the conference circuit (Deutsche Bank on 6/5), which reads like damage control rather than a narrative reset.

views.note: The +7.6% earnings reaction is the strongest in the universe and suggests a durable positive tone shift around cloud/AI execution.
Post-earnings +3.2% move on 5/28 confirms constructive sentiment, though crowded positive positioning tempers my confidence slightly.
A -22.4% earnings shock followed by four executive departure/change filings in six weeks signals a deeply negative and still-deteriorating narrative.
The -3.7% earnings reaction and subsequent conference presentation suggest management is trying to stabilize sentiment, but the tone has not yet turned.
A +4.0% earnings-day move and steady subsequent filings indicate positive tone, though the signal is now nearly two months old and likely priced.
The -3.7% post-earnings drop on 5/2 was notable, but the subsequent 'Other Events' filing on 5/12 lacks enough detail to confirm a continued negative narrative shift.
A modest +1.7% earnings reaction and a flurry of 'Other Events' filings suggest stable but unremarkable sentiment with no clear directional catalyst.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Easing but Export-Control Overhang Keeps NVDA Risk Elevated; Oil Weakness Caps XOM Upside
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has fallen roughly 13% over three months to 340.80, and VIX has dropped 22% in the past month to 18.48, suggesting the market is pricing in a de-escalation of near-term policy shocks. However, the level of uncertainty remains historically elevated, and HY OAS has widened 30 bp over three months to 3.18%, signaling that credit markets still see residual risk—likely tied to ongoing tariff and export-control regimes affecting semiconductor and industrial supply chains. NVDA's April 8-K (8.01 Other Events) coincides with the period of tightened AI-chip export restrictions to China, which I view as a structural headwind rather than a one-quarter event. WTI at $64.06 is down nearly 4% over three months despite a one-month bounce, reflecting soft global demand expectations that limit XOM's earnings trajectory. I would need a formal rollback of semiconductor export controls or a credible US-China trade framework to upgrade NVDA, and sustained OPEC+ cuts driving WTI above $75 to turn constructive on XOM.

views.note: Structural US-China AI-chip export controls remain the dominant geopolitical risk; April 8-K likely related to charge or disclosure around restricted shipments.
Supply-chain concentration in China is a known risk, but declining VIX and policy uncertainty suggest no imminent escalation; May 8-K provides no directional signal.
WTI at $64 and down 3.8% over three months reflects weak global demand; energy security tailwinds are offset by soft pricing, keeping me sidelined.
Tariff uncertainty could benefit domestic infrastructure spending but also raises input costs; two recent 8-Ks suggest active disclosure but I lack detail to take a directional view.
Steeper 10y-2y spread (+19 bp over 3m) and tightening HY OAS over the past month support bank earnings; geopolitical risk is manageable for a diversified US bank.
Multiple 8-Ks in April-May suggest active regulatory or strategic disclosures; antitrust and China ad-market exposure keep me neutral until clarity improves.
Defensive consumer staple with global supply-chain diversification; declining policy uncertainty supports stable demand, and three recent 8-Ks suggest proactive investor communication.
